title: SCIM hybrid provisioning wavefronts and lease-based deprovision failsafe
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Customers have reported prolonged inconsistencies between their identity provider and Redwood when large orgs perform directory changes (mass user deletes / group edits). Current SCIM workers run full batch passes which cause long tails, noisy error rates, and occasional premature deprovisions when transient failures occur. We need a robust provisioning architecture that reduces user-visible outages, provides deterministic retries, and retains forensic audit trails for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Incremental wave-based provisioning that splits large syncs into monotonic waves with configurable concurrency per-tenant
Lease-based deprovision gating: mark candidates as soft-deprovisioned (lease) and only finalize after N successful checks or TTL expiry
Idempotent operation tokens for each provisioning action to avoid duplicate creations/deletions across retries
Retry policy with capped exponential backoff + tenant-aware rate limits and a dead-letter queue for manual remediation
Audit log entries for every state transition (provisioned -> lease -> finalized / reclaimed) containing request-id, idempotency token, source-idp, and initiating webhook/cron
Observability: per-tenant SLA dashboards (lag, retry-rate, DLQ size), SLO alerts for stuck leases older than X hours
Security review completed and no elevation of privileges required to operate the lease machine
design_notes: Approach: implement 'wavefront' orchestrator that slices incoming SCIM deltas into sequential waves (configurable window size) so we can apply backpressure without blocking smaller tenants

Lease model: on first delete event mark user as LEASED with expiry TTL (default 48h). While leased, user is flagged in account store but auth remains functional except for high-risk operations. Final deletion only happens after lease confirms no re-provisioning requests or explicit admin confirmation.

Idempotency: generate operation_id = sha256(tenant+resource+event_timestamp) for all outbound calls to identity suppliers and internal workers. Persist last-seen operation_id per resource to reject duplicates.

Retry orchestration: use tenant-aware token bucket for retries to avoid a noisy tenant consuming worker capacity. Backoff uses capped exponential with full jitter. After 5 failed attempts push to DLQ with metadata for manual remediation.
Audit logging: write structured audit events to internal audit stream (append-only) with schema v2: {event_type, tenant_id, resource_type, operation, outcome, op_id, src}
Compatibility: compatible with both webhook-initiated and delta-sync modes; will prioritize webhook events to avoid delaying live changes
Edgecases: concurrent group membership churn requires ordered reconciliation: group edits are turned into delta operations with sequence numbers and reconciler ensures ordering per-group id
implementation_steps: 1) Prototype wavefront orchestrator as a sidecar to current SCIM-sync worker; add config flags for window_size and parallelism
2) Add lease state to user/group metadata in provisioning DB (states: ACTIVE, LEASED, FINALIZING, DELETED). Migrations: add column with default ACTIVE
3) Implement idempotency store in Redis with TTL > lease TTL; add checks to worker before executing destructive ops
4) Implement tenant-aware retry throttler and DLQ producer; DLQ messages include op_id, raw_scim_event, last_error
5) Instrument audit events; wire to existing audit-log pipeline and add parsers in Console to surface lease transitions
6) Add canary with 3 low-volume enterprise tenants for two weeks; capture metrics and iterate
7) Run security review and tabletop incident simulation for accidental mass-deletes
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Lease TTL too long => customer confusion. Mitigation: surface lease state in Console UI and in SCIM response metadata so admins can see pending deletions
Risk: DLQ backlog growth under burst. Mitigation: add per-tenant DLQ quotas and auto-escalation policy to SRE/SE teams
Risk: Inconsistent ordering for group reconciles. Mitigation: attach sequence numbers and perform idempotent merge operations in group store
Risk: Audit floods increase storage costs. Mitigation: sample low-risk events for verbose payloads while keeping minimal lineage for all events
